You start with a minimalist grid of gray tiles. Your goal is to click tiles to flip their colors between gray and white until the number of white tiles in every row and column exactly matches the required target numbers.

The challenge lies in the chain reaction constraint: whenever you flip a tile, its adjacent orthogonal neighbors will also flip their states. This creates a halo effect that requires you to plan ahead and see the big picture.

Features:
- Campaign mode with 100 levels spread across 10 chapters.
- Infinite random generation mode with dynamic difficulties from beginner 4x4 boards to expert 8x8 setups.
- Specialized rules such as frozen blocks that cannot be flipped and symmetry constraints.
- Clean, minimalist aesthetic utilizing black, white, and gray tones.
- No network connection required, completely offline gameplay.
- No intrusive permissions. A minimalist logic puzzle. Flip tiles, trigger chain reactions, match targets.

1. Game Intro
A relaxing one-touch puzzle game. The ball slides forward automatically after you control it.The ball can only move in straight lines: up, down, left, right. No diagonal moves, no turning mid-slide. Collect all coins and travel through all left and right paths to clear the level.
2. How to Play
No tapping, no long press. Swipe the screen in any straight direction. The ball will slide automatically in a straight line. The ball cannot change direction while moving. Wait until the ball stops, then swipe again. Diagonal swipes will not work.
3. Win Conditions (Must complete both)
1. Collect all coins: The ball automatically picks up coins on contact. You cannot leave any coins behind.
2. Pass all left and right passages: Move through every path on the map. Do not skip any roads or avoid any passages.
4. Game Over Rules
You fail the level if the ball slides out of bounds, gets stuck in a dead corner, leaves coins uncollected, or misses any passage. The level will restart automatically.
5. Game Tips
Look at the coin positions and paths first before sliding. Try to collect coins and clear paths in one straight move to avoid extra steps. Swipe gently on narrow roads to stay safe. Always double-check leftover coins and hidden small paths before finishing.
6. Warm Tips
No time limit, no in-app purchases. Play anytime and enjoy a relaxing sliding puzzle experience at your own pace. Slide the ball, collect all coins, clear all paths to win.

games.name: LayerTap - Stack Peel Puzzle
games.description: LayerTap presents a vertical stack of coloured layers viewed from the side. Each layer shows a number counting how many taps it takes to break through. Tap any layer and its count drops by one. When a layer reaches zero it shatters and disappears, and the layers above fall down to fill the gap. Four layer types keep every stack fresh. Normal layers just need taps. Gold layers are worth triple points but shatter faster. Crumble layers deal damage to the layers directly above and below when they break, potentially triggering a chain of breaking layers at once. Hard layers are thick and require many more taps to get through. The goal of each level is to clear every layer from the stack using as few taps as possible. The stack grows taller and harder layers appear more frequently as you progress through levels. Score is awarded from layer point values with bonus points for efficient play. Tap through a stack of layers — each one peels away to reveal the next.

games.description:
Feather Rush is a tap-to-reveal puzzle grid where chickens stand in for mines. You're working a board of hidden tiles, trying to hit a score target before the timer runs out. Some tiles are empty and worth a small bump. Some hide coins, which jump your score in big chunks. Some hide chickens, and chickens are bad news — they scatter your points and waste your moves. Numbered tiles tell you how many chickens are sitting in the eight cells around them, so you spend a lot of time triangulating: this one says 2, that one says 1, the corner nobody's flipped yet is probably the safe one.

The pressure here is the timer. Classic minesweeper lets you sit and stare at a board for as long as you need. Feather Rush gives you about two minutes per mission and a score floor that grows with each level. Mission 1 asks for 600 points, which is easy enough that the game lets you find your footing. By the time you're a few levels in, you're calculating risk versus reward on every flip — is it worth chasing a number cluster when the clock is burning, or do I just gamble on the next row and hope.

The art softens what's underneath. Bright cartoon palette, blue sky, urban street backdrops, a winking rooster mascot on every mission card. The chickens you discover have little expressions. The coins jingle in. It's cute enough that losing doesn't sting too much, which is probably the point.

The achievement structure pulls you in different directions on the same board. Mine Whisperer wants you to clear the grid clean, no chickens hit. Tactical Mind wants you to flag every chicken correctly before winning. Feather Speed ​​wants the win with thirty seconds still on the clock. So you're not optimizing one variable — you can replay the same mission with a different goal in mind and it genuinely changes how you play it.

The daily bonus is a four-by-four tic-tac-toe pull against the house. You're X, the house is O, three in a row in any line, you take the pot. It's a quick palate cleanser between missions and a reason to come back daily.

Coins from missions feed a stats panel that tracks total score, average score, wins versus losses, and games played. There's an Achievements tab that ledgers the named goals — First Flight, Gold Rush, On Fire, Veteran. The progression isn't aggressive; it just sits there as a quiet record of what you've done. Levels unlock in order, so you can see the road ahead, and you can see what's still locked.

What it feels closest to is minesweeper that learned to be friendly, with a score target and a clock stapled on. The friendliness is real — the visuals don't lie. The underlying puzzle is still honest minesweeper deduction, with all the gambling that implies when the timer is shrinking and you've still got rows of unflipped tiles staring back at you. Chickens hide. Coins shine. The clock ticks anyway.

CONTENT THAT GOES DEEP
• Easy — 50 curated 4×4 puzzles, one fold. A gentle on-ramp.
• Medium — 1,824 puzzles, two folds. The heart of the journey.
• Hard — 52,464 puzzles, three folds. Territory for players who want to stay a while.
In all, more than 54,000 hand-curated, deterministic levels—no random filler.

A DAILY RITUAL
Every local midnight, the same four puzzles appear for everyone: one easy, two medium, one hard. Clear all four at three stars to earn a +200 perfect-daily bonus toward the global leaderboard. Miss a day? Tomorrow is a fresh sheet.

GLOBAL LEADERBOARDS
Compete on the all-time board or the weekly board that resets every Monday at 00:00 UTC. Pick a display name in Settings—no email, phone, or social login required to play.

CRAFTED TO FEEL QUIET AND PREMIUM
Paper-atelier visuals, a satisfying unfold animation, haptics you can tone down mid-puzzle, and optional audio controls without leaving the board. During gameplay, screen capture is limited so an in-progress daily stays yours. Optional morning reminder at 10:00—only if you want it.

FREE TO PLAY, FAIRLY
You get five lives that refill over time. Optional rewarded ads can help with an extra life or hints. Want every gate lifted and ads removed for good? God Mode and God Mode Plus are one-time unlocks—never a subscription.

Fold the paper. Predict the holes. Unfold the truth—one quiet puzzle at a time.

Can you outsmart the advanced AI, accurately choose the trump suit (Rang), and secure the consecutive tricks needed to claim a Court (Rung)?

WHY PLAY ROYAL RANG?
• Pure Skill & Strategy: No forced monetization or luck-based gimmicks. Your victories are earned through tactical card play, memory, and sharp instincts.
• Advanced Offline AI: No internet? No problem. Train your skills against smart, adaptive computer opponents that play like real people.
• Stunning Visuals: Immerse yourself in a luxurious royal environment featuring sharp graphics, smooth card animations, and an intuitive UI.
• Daily Rewards: Log in every day to claim your rewards, build your streak, and level up your player profile.

HOW TO PLAY:
1. The game begins with the dealer distributing 5 cards to each player.
2. The Trump Caller (Rang Caller) selects the trump suit based on their initial cards.

games.description:
Spider Solitaire: Soviet Cards — the classic Spider solitaire and a separate Spiderette mode in warm vintage styling. It suits fans of relaxed logic and strategy as well as anyone who needs a quick distraction for a few minutes.

Key features
• Soviet aesthetics: a collection of unique card sets with retro illustrations and a themed color palette.
• Multiple difficulty levels: Easy — 1 suit, Medium — 2 suits, Hard — 4 suits.
• Spiderette mode: a separate game variant with 7 piles (staggered/kerchief layout) played with 52 cards.
• Comfortable controls and optimization for all screens: PC, tablet, smartphone.
• One‑hand play: interface and controls adapted for holding your phone in one hand.
• Hints and undo moves to help you learn and correct mistakes.
• Offline mode — play without an internet connection.
• Statistics and records — track your best streaks and progress.


How to play (brief)
The goal is to assemble all sequences from King to Ace of a single suit and move them to the Home; the number of completed sequences depends on the selected mode (Spider/Spiderette).

Quick rules
• Move cards between piles, arranging them in descending order from top to bottom: King, Queen, Jack … 2, Ace. Sequences of the same suit can be moved as a unit.
• Classic Spider uses 104 cards and the standard 10‑pile layout.
• In Spiderette mode, the game uses 52 cards and a 7‑pile staggered/kerchief layout; the starting layout and deck size differ, but movement rules are the same.
• When no moves are available or you want to add more cards, click the undealt deck — one face‑up card will be dealt to each pile.
• Use Hints and Undo to learn and correct mistakes.

Why play
• Warm retro atmosphere and stylish Soviet illustrations.
• Great for short breaks, training logic and strategic thinking.
• Suitable for beginners (1‑suit mode) and for players seeking a serious challenge (4‑suit mode).
• Play offline and one‑handed on your phone.

CoilParty is a live puzzle race you play together in the same room.

One person starts a party. Everyone else joins by scanning a QR code or typing a short room code. The puzzle appears on every phone at the same moment, and the race is on. First to untangle the coil takes the round. Win enough rounds and you take the party.

And here is the twist that turns friends into rivals. The moment you are about to lock in your solution, anyone else in the party can spend a power up to shuffle your board. Watch their face the second their puzzle scrambles. Listen to the room erupt. The lead changes in the last two seconds of almost every round.

No accounts. No sign ups. No email. No password. You open the app and play.

Free forever. No ads. No in app purchases. No paywalls.

Built for the kind of moments where a normal board game would be too slow and a video call would feel weird. Pull it out at a dinner, a road trip pit stop, a classroom break, a family hangout, a long wait at the airport. As long as everyone has a phone, you have a party.

Fast to start. A party is live in under ten seconds.

Easy to teach. The whole game is one rule. Untangle the coil before anyone else does, and sabotage the player who is about to beat you.

Built for groups. Bring in your roommates, your cousins, your whole study group. Everyone races at once on their own screen, against the same puzzle.

Calm to look at. Warm colors, gentle motion, zero flashing ads, zero pop ups begging you to rate.

Respectful of your phone. Tiny download. Light on battery. No tracking ad networks. No data sold to anyone.

HOW A ROUND WORKS

1. Host taps Create Party. A six character code appears.
2. Everyone else taps Join and enters the code, or scans the QR.
3. The same puzzle drops on every device.
4. Race. Untangle. Shuffle your rivals. Beat the room.
5. Scoreboard updates live. Next round starts when the host is ready.

GOOD FOR

Family game nights. Friend hangouts. Couples on the couch. Classrooms. Office lunches. Bachelor and bachelorette parties. Long flights with cousins. Dorm rooms at midnight. Anywhere a group has phones and five minutes to spare.

WHAT IT DOES NOT DO

Ask for your email. Ask for your name. Send you push notifications you did not sign up for. Show ads between rounds. Lock content behind a subscription. Track you across other apps. Sell your data.

PRIVACY IN ONE SENTENCE

CoilParty does not collect personal information. Gameplay state is synced anonymously so devices in the same party stay in sync. Full policy at https://coilparty.web.app/privacy

Made by an indie developer. No publisher. No investors. No growth team writing manipulative copy. Just a puzzle game built to make the room laugh.

ZyloShift is played on a grid ranging from 3x3 up to 5x5. At the start of each stage, you are presented with a scrambled grid containing colored blocks and a single empty slot. Rather than restoring a static picture, you must manipulate the rows and columns so they meet the specific color sequence rules of that level.

games.name: Legend Chess Arena
games.description:
Chess Legends — Play Against History's Greatest Masters

What if you could sit across the board from Paul Morphy, the genius who never lost a serious game? Or feel the relentless pressure of Alekhine's attacking play? Chess Legends brings history's greatest players to life — each one faithfully recreated with their own unique style, strengths, and weaknesses.

PLAY AGAINST LEGENDARY MASTERS
Choose from 16 historical legends, each with a distinct playing style built from their real games and documented strategies:

- Paul Morphy — The romantic attacker who punished passive play
- Alexander Alekhine — Deep calculations and relentless initiative
- José R. Capablanca — Flawless technique and endgame precision
- Emanuel Lasker — Psychological mastery and fighting spirit
- Wilhelm Steinitz — The father of positional chess
- Aron Nimzowitsch — Prophylaxis and hypermodern strategy
- Richard Réti — Flexible piece play and flank openings
- Mikhail Chigorin — Knight lover and combinational genius
- Adolf Anderssen — The Immortal Game creator
- Akiba Rubinstein — The greatest rook endgame player of all time
- Harry Pillsbury — Systematic attack and piece coordination
- Carl Schlechter — Solid, balanced, and almost impossible to beat
- François-André Philidor — "Pawns are the soul of chess"
- Ruy López de Segura — The founding father of opening theory
- And more...

AUTHENTIC STYLE SIMULATION
Each legend doesn't just play good chess — they play *their* chess. Morphy develops pieces at lightning speed and punishes any passive move. Petrosian avoids weaknesses at all costs and neutralises your plans before you form them. Tal sacrifices material for complications, trusting chaos over calculation. The simulation goes deep: opening books built from real historical games, positional preferences, tactical tendencies, and even characteristic error patterns.

THREE DIFFICULTY LEVELS
Not ready to face Capablanca? Start with Beginner, Normal, or Professional opponents to build your skills before challenging the legends.

POST-GAME ANALYSIS
After each game, review every move with engine-powered analysis. See your accuracy rating, identify blunders and brilliant moves, and understand exactly where the game turned.

ELO RATING SYSTEM
Track your progress with a personal Elo rating that updates after every game. Watch yourself grow as you defeat stronger and stronger opponents across history.

HISTORICAL CONTEXT
Each legend comes with their era, playing style, and Elo equivalent — giving you a window into 500 years of chess history, from Ruy López in 16th-century Spain to Alekhine's combinations in the 1930s.

CLEAN, FOCUSED EXPERIENCE
No ads. No distractions. Just you and the board.

Chess Legends is for players who love chess history and want more than a rating number — they want to understand how the game evolved and feel what it was like to face the greatest minds the game has ever produced. Chess Legends — Play against history's greatest chess masters

games.name: ChessMonsters
subcategories: Chess for Kids Ages 6 and Up
games.description:
Does your child love games and you want to introduce them to chess in a playful way? Monster Chess does exactly that – with colorful monster pieces, simple rules, and an AI that adapts to your child's skill level.
LEARN CHESS WITHOUT FRUSTRATION
Chess can feel intimidating. Monster Chess solves that in the simplest way: the pieces aren't silent wooden blocks, but lively monster characters with personality. Kids instantly understand who's on their team and who's the opponent – and almost start playing on their own.
FOUR DIFFICULTY LEVELS
Baby Monster: The dark team plays intentionally badly. Kids win almost every time and build confidence.
Sleepy Dragon: Random moves, very easy. Perfect for practicing the basic rules.
Angry Wolf: The monster starts capturing pieces. A real challenge for kids with some experience.
Evil Wizard: Simple strategy for kids who already know their way around the board.
100% SAFE FOR KIDS
No ads. No internet. No account. No tracking. No in-app purchases. Monster Chess runs entirely on the device – no outside connections. The parent area is protected by a simple math problem so kids can't accidentally change settings.
FOR PARENTS
As a parent you know: the best games are the ones where kids don't even realize they're learning. Monster Chess teaches your child all the basic rules of chess – pawns, knights, bishops, rooks, queens, kings – without learning pressure and without screen-time guilt.
Chess builds logical thinking, focus, and patience. And with Monster Chess, it's actually fun.
Buy once. No subscription. Play forever. Learn chess the fun way – with monster pieces, no ads, no internet, no subscription. Buy once, play forever. Chess for Kids Ages 6 and Up
